reference.source: Thomas Bulkowski, The Pattern Site — Double Top (Adam & Adam), Identification Guidelines

fires.our_rule: the newest two same-kind confirmed swings from `detect_market_structure` at hard-coded `lookback: 2` (events.rs:1083) within `tolerance_pct: 0.004` (patterns.rs:135), with any confirmed opposite swing between them; fires on the pattern's GEOMETRY, with no close-below-the-valley requirement, and re-fires every bar the pair stays newest; price = the valley (entry_level), zone = [target, invalidation], magnitude = 0.5+0.5*equality (patterns.rs:274-337)
fires.their_rule: two peaks with a valley between, "the double top confirms as a true double top once price closes below the valley"; Bulkowski also asks for a valley drop of at least 10% and peak variation usually under 3%

reference.source: Thomas Bulkowski, The Pattern Site — Bulkowski on the Head-and-Shoulders Chart Pattern
reference.quote: A neckline is a trendline that connects the two armpits of a head-and-shoulders pattern.

draw.today: 2 horizontal `Line`s at 79764.01 — the neckline — 49 and 51px wide, dy 0, at bars 290-291 of 501, each labelled `head_shoulders`. fires.our_rule: the three newest confirmed swing highs and two lows interleaved shoulder-trough-head-trough-shoulder, shoulders within `tolerance_pct 0.004` of the head price and the head above both by that tol (patterns.rs:187-231); neckline = the FLAT MINIMUM of the two troughs, not the line joining them; fires on geometry alone — no close-below-neckline condition — re-firing every bar while the five swings stay newest; inverse H&S maps to the same concept id with Side::Buy (events.rs:1096); only tops fired this window (2 bearish events)
fires.their_rule: three peaks with the middle highest and roughly equal shoulders; "a neckline is a trendline that connects the two armpits"; the pattern confirms when price closes below the neckline and projects the head's height beyond it

rule_as_data.rule: swings(lookback=2): 3 highs + 2 lows interleaved, shoulders within 0.4% of head, head highest => emit(flat_neckline=min(troughs), zone=[target, invalidation], every bar while newest)

reference.source: Thomas Bulkowski, The Pattern Site — Symmetrical Triangles
reference.quote: Two trendlines bound prices; the bottom trendline slopes up and the top one slopes down.

draw.today: 50 horizontal `Line`s at 8 distinct levels (19-114px, dy 0), every one in the NEUT slate because the detector hard-codes `PatternDirection::Neutral` (patterns.rs:371) and the router has no side to colour from, plus 50 copies of the word `triangle`.
